# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 86 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 86 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_086_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 3

**1** I saw a tall man come and call the virgins, walking around the tower and examining it very carefully. He handed the virgins a rod and they began to strike the tower with it. **2** The tower shook throughout, and the parts that were not sound fell away; but the sound parts remained firm. **3** I marveled when I saw the tower shaken, for it had been built of such glorious stones. **4** And he said to me, "Do not be troubled; for the tower is being shaken in order that those who are unsound may fall away and those who are sound may remain." **5** Then the tall man said to the virgins, "Remove from the tower any stones that are unsound, and deliver them to the builders." The removed stones were found to be of various kinds: some were round, smooth, and polished, not fitting into the tower; others were cracked; others were rough; others were white and round, unsuitable for the building. **6** I saw the virgins remove some stones from the tower and lay them aside. Then they went to the gate and brought other stones from there to fit in their place. **7** But other stones were not brought from the gate; they remained by the roadside, and all who had placed them there took them back. **8** He said to me, "Those stones removed from the tower and placed by the roadside — you see the round ones. If they do not repent, they shall find no place in the building; but if they repent and are found worthy, they shall be built into the tower. But if they do not repent, they shall be replaced by others, and these shall be cast out utterly." **9** When I had seen all this, the shepherd said to me, "Come, let us withdraw a little, and when the virgins have finished the tower, I will explain to you the meaning of all this." **10** So I withdrew a short distance with him, and the virgins completed the rest of the building.

---

### Translator's Note
The testing of the tower by shaking (v. 2) mirrors the testing of believers through affliction — the round stones cannot fit the square tower because worldliness (symbolized by roundness, which has no flat stable face) makes believers unable to be incorporated into the community. The pattern of removal and possible re-insertion reflects the Shepherd's persistent theme of post-baptismal repentance. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
